battle.name: 羅藝起事
battle.brief: 大業十二年（616）歲末，幽州總管羅藝舉兵脫離隋廷，據薊縣柳城一線，以騎兵屯田自給，與涿郡高開道一系在城郊爭鋒，後為竇建德、唐所封拜。卡面這件羅馬短劍屬公元前一百年的量產制式佩劍，此役無一字記載，它所標示的是邊軍守城、以盾緣咬合刺突那一類近身兵器。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 大業末年的河北北部，衝突的一方是隋朝中央與以幽州總管羅藝為首的幽州邊軍勢力。隋廷此時的指揮體系已從開皇年間的府兵制上滑落：尚書省兵部只餘符印與軍籍之權，調兵靠行軍總管、總管、判官逐級傳令，郡縣以太守、令領郡兵縣兵應敵，邊郡另有屯田戍卒與護防兵；大業年間三次征高句麗與連年巡幸把府兵抽空，募兵、逃戶、降附部眾被混編充數，隊伍的裝備與紀律參差不齊。幽州方面，羅藝以邊鎮總管的身份一手掌握薊縣與柳城一線的城防、屯田、馬政與徵發，麾下是北方邊軍的騎兵、步兵與胡漢混編的部曲，馬匹來自塞外互市與北部牧場，糧秣靠屯田與薊縣周邊的轉輸，訊息靠邊塞烽燧逐段傳遞。第三方同樣在場：北面是契丹與靺鞨的游騎，隨時越塞抄掠；西面是竇建德治下的河北與渤海；同期在涿郡一帶起兵的另一支河北武裝高開道，則是羅藝在幽州城下最直接的敵手。局勢演成隋、羅藝、高開道、竇建德四方在河北與塞北互相爭奪，隨著江都變局與關中入唐，才逐步收束。
countriesEn: In the far north of Hebei in the closing years of the Daye reign, one side of the conflict was the Sui court at the centre and, on the other, the frontier force of Youzhou under its commandant, Luo Yi. By that time the Sui command system had slid a long way from the fubing establishment of the Kaihuang era: under the Ministry of War only the tallies and the personnel rolls retained real authority, troops were moved by travelling army commissioners, commandants and registrars passing orders down the chain, prefectures and counties answered with commandery and county levies under their administrators, and the frontier commanderies kept military farms, garrison settlers and protective troops besides. Three campaigns against Goguryeo and the repeated tours of the court had drained the fubing hollow, so hired soldiers, runaways and surrendered groups were mixed into the ranks to make up the numbers, and the equipment and drill of the resulting units were uneven. On the Youzhou side, Luo Yi held the military government of the northern border in his own hands as commandant of the commandery: the defences, the military farms, the horse administration and the levies of the Jixian and Liucheng line all answered to him. Under him served the horse and foot of the northern frontier together with retainers recruited from Chinese and non-Chinese alike; the horses came from the markets beyond the wall and from the pastures to the north, the grain from the military farms and the deliveries around Jixian, and the news travelled by beacon towers along the frontier stage by stage. Third parties were present as well. To the north the riders of the Khitan and the Mohe crossed the frontier and took cattle whenever they chose; to the west lay the Hebei and the Bohai under Dou Jiande; and in the Zuo commandery of the same region another armed rising, that of Gao Kaidao, was Luo Yi's most immediate rival before the walls of Youzhou. The situation settled into a four-cornered contest among the Sui, Luo Yi, Gao Kaidao and Dou Jiande for Hebei and the steppe beyond, and it was only the upheaval at Jiangdu and the rise of the Tang in Guanzhong that closed it down.
people: 羅藝是這場衝突的主角，幽州（薊縣）人，家世宿於北方軍鎮，父祖皆任邊州武職，他以行伍出身在隋末繼領幽州總管。史籍對他起事的過程記得很省，詳細經過要靠《資治通鑑》卷百八十五、百八十六與《舊唐書》《新唐書》羅藝傳互相參校，可以確定的是他手裡握著幽州一帶的兵權、馬政與城防。隋煬帝楊廣是這場衝突的另一端，他本人遠在江都與洛陽之間巡行，對幽州只能以詔令徵兵徵糧、遣使責問，實際指揮全落在幽州與河北各州的守將手上。宇文化及是關鍵的第三方：他在江都弒隋煬帝、另立新主，幽州一線是否奉詔，直接決定羅藝起兵的時機與名分。竇建德在河北收拾潰兵流民，最早看出幽州這支部隊的價值，隋亡之後以燕郡王封羅藝；李淵則在大業十三年（617）於太原起兵，兩年之後羅藝轉而投向唐。幽州出身的將佐是另一條值得留意的線：秦瓊字叔寶，隋末在羅藝麾下任職，因羅藝畏忌而投奔裴仁基部，其同族羅士信亦為隋將，後隨唐軍征討劉黑闥；兩人由幽州軍鎮進入唐軍序列，說明羅藝部眾的骨幹後來成了唐初北方軍隊的重要來源。高開道是羅藝多年的宿敵，兩家在幽州城郊反覆拉鋸，直到貞觀年間才由唐軍平定。至於羅藝之死，事由在史籍中說法不一：貞觀九年（634），他被以謀反罪賜死，一說與統軍丘行則陰謀叛逆，一說則是御史糾舉其驕恣怨望、朝廷藉此收其兵權。
peopleEn: Luo Yi is the protagonist of this conflict. He was a man of Youzhou, that is of Jixian, his family long settled in the northern military towns, his forebears holding martial posts on the border commanderies; he came up through the ranks and in the last years of the Sui took command of Youzhou. The records are sparing about the rising itself, and its course has to be reconstructed by collating the Comprehensive Mirror in juan 185 and 186 with the biography of Luo Yi in the Old and New Tang histories. What can be fixed is that he held the command, the horse administration and the defences of the Youzhou line. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, stands at the other end of the conflict, but he was far away, touring between Jiangdu and Luoyang, and all he could do to Youzhou was to issue edicts calling up men and grain and to send envoys to upbraid; the actual command lay with the defending officers of Youzhou and of the prefectures of Hebei. Yuwen Huaji was the decisive third party: having killed Emperor Yang at Jiangdu and set up a new ruler, he made the question of whether the Youzhou line obeyed his orders the very thing that fixed the timing and the legitimacy of Luo's rising. Dou Jiande, gathering broken troops and runaway peasants in Hebei, was the first to see the worth of this force; after the fall of the Sui he ennobled Luo Yi as Prince of Yan, while Li Yuan, who rose at Taiyuan in the thirteenth year of Daye, that is 617, drew him over to the Tang two years later. The officers who came out of Youzhou form another line worth following: Qin Qiong, courtesy name Shubao, held office under Luo Yi in the last years of the Sui and, because Luo Yi feared and disliked him, went over to the command of Pei Renji; his kinsman Luo Shixin was likewise a Sui officer and later campaigned against Liu Heita with the Tang. The fact that men like these moved from the Youzhou commandery into the Tang order of battle shows that the backbone of Luo's troops later became an important source of the Tang's northern armies. Gao Kaidao was Luo's long-standing enemy, and the two fought over the ground outside Youzhou city again and again until the Tang finally settled the matter in the Zhenguan era. As for the end of Luo's own life, the histories differ: in the ninth year of Zhenguan, 634, he was put to death on a charge of plotting rebellion, some accounts holding that he had conspired with the officer in command Qiu Xingze, others that the censors had impeached him for arrogance and resentment and the court had seized his troops on that pretext.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬短劍屬公元前一百年的制式佩劍，與616年的幽州沒有直接交涉，這一點必須先講清楚：它不曾出現在薊縣的城頭上。但把它放回它所屬的體系裡看，仍能說出它與這場衝突的關係。羅馬短劍是雙刃、窄身、尖鋒、全長約六十公分、刃長約三十五至四十五公分、重量約一公斤的短刺劍，靠兵工坊成批打造，供基層士兵佩用；它配的是大盾，而不是可以揮砍的長刀，羅馬人用盾的邊緣卡住對方的刺擊，再以短劍順著盾面捅入，甲胄接縫、腋下與咽喉成為固定的刺擊目標。中國那邊與它同一位置的武器是隋唐的佩刀：環首刀為主流，直刃無環首的刀在隋代亦已出現，形制短而厚重，與短劍同樣是步兵、射手與軍官的隨身佩刀，須用單手拔出揮刺；與之配合的是長槊、大盾與拒馬槊，而不是能縱橫劈砍的長刀。換言之，隋軍在城門衝撞、甬道接戰與步騎混戰中近身廝殺所倚賴的，正是短刺刀加大盾這一套。攻城手段則各有名堂：隋軍備雲梯、撞車、巢車、火箭與床弩，幽州城外的攻防靠壕壘、壍道與投石器械相持；羅馬人攻城時攜帶短劍，也正是因為城門、階梯與甬道裡沒有揮砍的空間。除兵器之外，幽州軍的戰馬來自塞外互市、渤海與柳城牧場，羅藝部的機動全靠騎兵；運輸靠畜力車隊與屯田所出糧秣，糧道自薊縣通往柳城、漁陽與塞外戍所，冬季以雪車與牛羊馱運，軍中的日用則靠屯田自給，長途不需就地徵斂。
kitsEn: The Roman short sword on this card is a standard issue weapon of the year 100 BC and has no direct connection with Youzhou in 616, and that has to be said plainly at the start: it never appeared on the walls of Jixian. Set back in the system to which it belongs, however, its bearing on this conflict can still be stated. The Roman gladius is double-edged, narrow, tapering to a point, about sixty centimetres in all, with a blade of thirty-five to forty-five centimetres and a weight of roughly one kilogram; it was turned out in batches by the arsenal workshops and issued to the men of the line. It was carried with a large shield and not with a long blade that could be swung: the Romans caught an opponent's thrust on the edge of the shield and then drove the short sword in along the face of it, so that the seams of the armour, the armpit and the throat became the fixed targets. The Chinese counterpart in the same slot is the sabre of the Sui and the Tang: the ring-pommel dao was the standard, and the straight-bladed dao without a ring pommel already appears in the Sui, short and heavy in construction, and like the gladius it was the sidearm of foot soldiers, archers and officers alike, drawn and thrust with a single hand; it worked together with the long spear, the large shield and the anti-cavalry bristling spear, and not with a blade that could be swung in a wide arc. In other words, when the Sui army closed to hand-to-hand work at a breached gate, in a passage or in the mixed fighting of foot and horse, what it relied upon was precisely this pairing of a short stabbing blade with a shield. The means of siege had their own names on each side: the Sui brought scaling ladders, battering rams, siege towers, fire arrows and heavy crossbows, and the contest before Youzhou was carried on with ditches, rampart roads and stone-throwing engines; the Romans took their short swords into assaults precisely because there was no room to swing inside a gate, on a stair or in a passage. Beyond the weapons, the horses of the Youzhou army came from the markets beyond the wall, from the Bohai coast and from the pastures of Liucheng, and the mobility of Luo's command rested entirely on cavalry. Transport was by draught animals and by the grain of the military farms, the grain road running from Jixian to Liucheng, to Yuyang and to the garrison posts beyond the wall, with sledges and oxen and sheep carrying it in winter, while the daily food of the army came from its own farms and did not have to be squeezed out of the countryside.
tactics: 羅藝起事後的作戰樣式，與其說是一場攻城戰，不如說是一場以邊軍為骨架的割據防衛。起事初期靠的是營壘與城：薊縣城是隋在北方最堅固的城防之一，內有倉城、軍器庫與水源，羅藝據城以拒隋廷派來的討伐軍與使節，把城外的騎兵分作數部，用以遮斷官軍的糧道與徵發隊伍。與高開道一系在城郊的拉鋸更能看出邊軍的特點：雙方都避免強攻城池，而以騎兵在曠野上互相咬截，勝負多取決於誰能先偵知對方的集結地，誰的弓弩陣能先壓住騎兵衝鋒的落點。隋廷的平叛則沿用它擅長的辦法：調各郡縣之兵，募河南與山東的散卒，派行軍總管統率，先斷糧再合圍；然而616年的中原精銳已被瓦崗與張須陀的戰事吸住，關中與江都兩端又各有變局，能真正壓到幽州去的兵力有限，這正是羅藝能站住腳跟的關鍵。攻守之間，短兵器的作用被放大：城門被撞開的瞬間、甬道裡的接戰、盾陣被擠壓的瞬間，都是刺擊而不是揮砍的場合，短刺刀加大盾的組合在此發揮作用；而攻城一方能倚靠的則是長槊、弩、撞車與火箭。起事軍的補給靠屯田、芻草與城內存糧，不靠臨時徵發，與那些流動的農民起義不同，這使它能承受長期圍困而不致崩散。
tacticsEn: The way Luo Yi fought after the rising began was less a siege than a partition of the border guarded by the frontier army itself. In the first stage the rising rested on the camp and on the city: Jixian was among the strongest defences the Sui possessed in the north, with its grain store, its armoury and its wells inside, and Luo Yi held the city against the punitive columns and envoys sent by the Sui court, dividing the cavalry outside into several bodies whose business was to cut the grain road and the columns of levies the other side was sending out. The running fight with Gao Kaidao's people on the ground outside the city shows the character of a frontier army even more plainly: neither side was willing to assault a walled town directly, and instead the horse met the horse on the open plain, the result turning mainly on who first learned where the other was massed and whose line of bows and crossbows could break the fall of a charge first. The Sui court's method of putting the rising down followed the routine it knew: to draw on the levies of the commanderies and counties, to hire scattered men in Henan and Shandong, to send a travelling army commissioner to take command, to cut the supplies and then to close in. But the best troops of the central plains were in 616 already tied up against the Wagang band and against the fighting of Zhang Xuetuo, while Guanzhong and Jiangdu each had their own emergencies, and the force that could really be pressed against Youzhou was thin. That was the key to Luo's ability to hold his ground. Between attack and defence the role of the short blade grew: the instant a gate was forced, the moment of contact in a passage, the moment when a shield line was pressed together were all occasions for stabbing and not for swinging, and that was where the pairing of short sword and shield did its work; what the assaulting side could lean on was the long spear, the crossbow, the ram and the fire arrow. The supply of the rebel force came from the military farms, from fodder and from the grain stored inside the walls rather than from ad hoc levies, and that set it apart from the shifting peasant risings and allowed it to bear a long siege without dissolving.
data: 有據可查的數字不多，逐一列出。時間：事繫於隋煬帝大業十二年（616）歲末，也有史家繫於大業十三年（617）初，兩說並存，卡面繫年取616。行政：隋幽州治薊縣，即今北京，據《隋書·地理志》領十九縣，東有漁陽、薊東與柳城之塞，西有居庸、軍都諸關隘。距離：薊縣至榆關約二百五十公里，至柳城約三百五十公里，至太原晉陽約六百公里，至長安一千一百公里以上；羅藝的援應線與竇建德的河北、與唐的關中，都靠這幾百公里的距離拉開時間差。城池：幽州城周約二十餘里，內築倉城、軍器庫與井泉，城外有壘、壕與烽燧環繞。兵制數字：隋三次征高句麗，每次發兵以數十萬計，士卒死亡以數十萬計，府兵編制在十餘年間被抽空，616年時全國能戰之兵相對有限；羅藝軍的具體兵額史無明文，只能從邊軍的常備規模與後來唐廷對其部的安置去推想。壽命：羅藝起事在隋亡之前，618年竇建德以燕郡王封之，619年羅藝投向唐，受任幽州大都督，634年貞觀九年以謀反罪賜死。可作對照的器械數字：羅馬短劍全長約六十公分、刃長約三十五至四十五公分、重量約一公斤，單手持握；隋的環首刀與直刃刀長度多在六十至八十公分之間，重量相仿，兩套形制在尺寸與分量上幾乎可以互相對譯，但相隔一千七百餘年。
dataEn: The figures that can actually be vouched for are few, and they are set out one by one. On time: the affair belongs to the end of the twelfth year of Daye under Emperor Yang of Sui, that is 616, though some historians place it at the beginning of the thirteenth year, 617; both readings exist, and the card takes 616. On administration: the Sui commandery of Youzhou had its seat at Jixian, that is at present-day Beijing, and according to the geography chapter of the Book of Sui it governed nineteen counties, with Yuyang and the passes of Liucheng to the east and the defiles of Juyong and Jundun to the west. On distance: from Jixian it is about two hundred and fifty kilometres to the pass at Yulinshan, about three hundred and fifty to Liucheng, about six hundred to Jinyang in Taiyuan and more than eleven hundred to Chang'an; the lines of supply by which Luo Yi could be reached, whether from Dou Jiande's Hebei or from the Tang in Guanzhong, were all set by a separation of several hundred kilometres. On the city: the walls of Youzhou ran about twenty-odd li in circuit, with a grain store, an armoury and wells inside, and ramparts, ditches and beacon towers around it. On the military system: the Sui campaigned against Goguryeo three times, raising armies counted in the tens of thousands on each occasion and counting the dead in the tens of thousands, and the fubing establishment was hollowed out within a dozen years, so that the empire in 616 had relatively little manpower left that could fight; no figure survives for the strength of Luo's army, and it can only be inferred from the standing size of a frontier command and from the way the Tang court later settled his troops. On the life span of the affair: the rising began before the Sui fell; in 618 Dou Jiande ennobled him as Prince of Yan; in 619 Luo Yi came over to the Tang and was appointed commandant of Youzhou; in 634, the ninth year of Zhenguan, he was put to death on a charge of plotting rebellion. As a set of figures for comparison, the weapons: the Roman short sword was about sixty centimetres in all, with a blade of thirty-five to forty-five centimetres, weighed about a kilogram and was held in one hand; the ring-pommel and straight dao of the Sui ran mostly between sixty and eighty centimetres and weighed comparably. The two types can very nearly be translated into one another in size and weight, though they are separated by more than seventeen hundred years.
cause: 直接導火線是616年歲末幽州與中央之間的決裂：大業年間國家把幽州這樣的邊鎮當作可以任意徵發的倉庫，兵要徵、馬要徵、糧芻要徵，供洛陽與江都兩端的巡幸與戰事使用，而邊軍自己的待遇卻沒有相應保障，遼東與塞北的防線也因精銳被抽走而空虛，契丹與靺鞨的游騎因此年年越塞。郡縣催督的使者往來其急，羅藝既握兵柄又掌馬政，便有了不必再忍的理由；同一條邊防線上，涿郡的高開道等部眾也在起兵，彼此刺激，河北北部的武裝化由此加速。深一層的背景是隋朝整體的崩解：大業十年到十四年（614至618）三次征高句麗之後，役繁、兵疲、逃戶滿州，糧價騰貴，民間讖語與歌謠在河北山東流傳，講的是劉氏當有天下，人心早已不耐朝廷的徵斂。這樣的背景下，羅藝的起事並非只有羅藝一人的野心，也是邊軍、屯田戶與州縣胥吏在共同壓力下的一次集體選擇：一個能打、能守、又能自己供得起給養的邊鎮，寧可自己當家，也不再等江都與洛陽的詔書。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the breach between Youzhou and the centre at the end of 616. Throughout the Daye reign the state treated a frontier commandery such as Youzhou as a warehouse to be drawn on at will: men were called up, horses were called up, grain and fodder were called up, all of it to feed the tours and the wars of the court at Luoyang and at Jiangdu, while the frontier army itself received no corresponding security; the defensive lines in Liaodong and beyond the wall were hollowed out as the picked troops were drawn away, and the riders of the Khitan and the Mohe accordingly crossed the frontier year after year. The envoys who came to press the commanderies hurried back and forth, and Luo Yi, holding both the command of troops and the administration of horses, had reason enough not to endure it any longer. On the same frontier line the bands of Gao Kaidao and others in the Zuo commandery were also rising, and the two stirred each other, so that the militarisation of northern Hebei quickened. A deeper background is the general dissolution of the Sui: after the three campaigns against Goguryeo between 614 and 618, the corvée was heavy, the soldiers were tired, runaways filled every prefecture and the price of grain rose sharply, while prophecies and songs telling that a house surnamed Liu would hold the realm circulated through Hebei and Shandong, and the mood of the people had long ceased to endure the court's exactions. In that setting Luo's rising was not the private ambition of Luo Yi alone; it was a collective choice made under common pressure by the frontier soldiers, the military-farm households and the clerks of the prefectures. A border town that could fight, could hold its walls and could feed itself from its own fields would rather keep its own house in order than go on waiting for edicts from Jiangdu and Luoyang.
impact: 這場起事的第一層影響在河北與東北的地緣上：隋廷失去薊縣與柳城這個北方樞紐，幽州從朝廷的邊郡變成事實上的割據勢力，河北與塞北的權力真空被打開，高開道趁勢坐大，唐初因此在北方邊地捱了十餘年的拉鋸，從619年羅藝歸唐到貞觀四年（630）高開道覆滅，前後十一年，北方邊線始終未能完全安寧。第二層影響在軍隊與人事上：羅藝降唐時帶來的是一支可以直接使用的北方邊軍——熟習塞外地形的騎兵、能自給的屯田與城防體系、以及一批幽州出身的將佐，秦瓊與羅士信正是在這個體系裡長成唐初名將；唐廷得以用最少的關中兵源去經營幽州一線，倚靠的正是羅藝留下的這套人馬與法令。第三層是唐初政治中的隱憂：羅藝手握重兵、封爵且驕恣，終於在貞觀九年被以謀反罪處置，其部眾被拆散編入唐軍，幽州由軍鎮自雄轉為朝廷直轄，這條由隋末邊軍割據開出的傳統，自此成為歷代北方邊鎮治理要處理的難題。最後是文學與民間記憶：羅藝在《說唐》《隋唐演義》裡被寫成燕王，秦瓊一度在他麾下，義友萬修死在起兵之役——正史裡只有寥寥數語的幽州事變，反而靠說部留在了華夏記得的英雄故事裡。
impactEn: The first layer of consequence lies in the geography of Hebei and the northeast. The Sui court lost Jixian and Liucheng, the pivot of its northern frontier; Youzhou ceased to be a border commandery of the court and became in fact a power of its own; the vacuum in Hebei and in the country beyond the wall was opened up; Gao Kaidao grew fat in it; and the Tang therefore spent more than a decade of pulling and hauling on its northern frontier, from Luo's submission in 619 to the fall of Gao Kaidao in the fourth year of Zhenguan, 630, and for eleven years the northern line was never entirely quiet. The second layer lies in troops and in men. When Luo Yi came over to the Tang he brought with him a northern frontier army that could be used as it stood: cavalry that knew the ground beyond the wall, military farms that fed themselves, a system of frontier defences, and a set of officers who came from Youzhou. Qin Qiong and Luo Shixin grew into famous Tang commanders inside that very system, and it was on the strength of the men and the ordinances Luo Yi left behind that the Tang court was able to hold the Youzhou line with as few troops from Guanzhong as it did. The third layer is the anxiety of early Tang politics over its own commanders. Luo Yi held heavy troops, a title and an overbearing manner, and in the ninth year of Zhenguan he was put to death on a charge of plotting rebellion, his men broken up and incorporated into the Tang armies, and Youzhou turned from a self-willed military town into a commandery directly governed by the court; the tradition of the frontier commanderies that had opened under the late Sui became from then on one of the standing difficulties of governing the northern border. Last of all is the layer of literature and popular memory. In the Shuo Tang and the Sui Tang Yanyi Luo Yi is written as the Prince of Yan, Qin Qiong serves under him for a time, and the sworn brother Wan Xiu dies in the rising itself. An event of which the official histories preserve only a few lines has, through the storytellers, remained in the roll of heroic tales the Chinese remember.
result: 結果是起事成功，隋朝失去了幽州。羅藝擊退或驅散了朝廷派來徵發、責問的官軍與使者，據薊縣、柳城與周邊諸縣，自立為幽州之主，把一支邊軍變成自己的部曲；這一步跨出去之後，隋廷再沒有能力把幽州收回。隋亡之後，河北的竇建德最先看出這支部隊的份量，遣使封羅藝為燕郡王，羅藝一度倒向河北；大業十三年李淵在太原起兵、次年入長安之後，羅藝於619年率眾歸唐，受封燕郡王、拜幽州大都督，率舊部與唐軍一同征討高開道、劉黑闥，幽州遂成唐初北方最重要的一個軍鎮。事情在貞觀九年（634）轉了彎：羅藝以謀反罪賜死，兵權收歸朝廷，部眾分編各鎮，這場由邊軍反對中央徵發而起、終於被新王朝吸收的起事，就此收場。可以確定的是：616年之後，隋朝在河北北部的統治實際上已經終結；可以存疑的是羅藝起義的具體戰鬥經過、雙方兵數與勝負細節，正史皆無記載，只能由《資治通鑑》與《舊唐書》《新唐書》羅藝傳的零星記載，加上地勢、兵制與器械的限制去推想。卡面那件羅馬短劍自不曾到過薊縣，但它提示的東西卻實實在在：短刺劍加大盾的近戰邏輯，從羅馬的城門攻打到隋唐的城門攻防，兩千年並無二致。
resultEn: The result was success for the rising and the loss of Youzhou to the Sui. Luo Yi beat off or drove away the officers and envoys the court had sent to call up men and to upbraid him, held Jixian, Liucheng and the counties around them, made himself master of Youzhou and turned a frontier army into his own retainers; once that step had been taken the Sui court never had the strength to take Youzhou back. After the fall of the Sui, Dou Jiande of Hebei was the first to see what this force was worth, and sent an envoy to ennobble Luo Yi as Prince of Yan, and Luo Yi turned for a time toward Hebei. After Li Yuan rose at Taiyuan in the thirteenth year of Daye and entered Chang'an the following year, Luo Yi came over to the Tang with his men in 619, was ennobled as Prince of Yan and appointed commandant of Youzhou, and marched with the old troops alongside the Tang against Gao Kaidao and Liu Heita, so that Youzhou became the most important military town of the early Tang in the north. The affair took a different turn in the ninth year of Zhenguan, 634: Luo Yi was put to death on a charge of plotting rebellion, the command passed back to the court, and his men were distributed among the various commands, and the rising that had begun as a frontier army's resistance to the court's exactions and ended by being absorbed into a new dynasty was thereby closed. What can be fixed is this: after 616 the Sui's rule in northern Hebei was effectively finished. What remains uncertain is the actual course of Luo's rising, the numbers on either side and the details of who won and lost; the official histories preserve none of it, and it can only be inferred from the scattered notices in the Comprehensive Mirror and in the biography of Luo Yi in the Old and New Tang histories, together with the limits set by the terrain, the military system and the weapons. The Roman short sword on the card never reached Jixian, but the lesson it carries is a real one: the logic of stabbing with a short blade behind a shield, from the Roman assault on a gate to the Sui and Tang defence of one, is the same after two thousand years.
